layers.message: Move to pnpm workspaces on Node 22 and rename shared to money

graderOnly: .standards/CONTEXT.md was written for the earlier signed-off cycle add-due-dates-to-invoices-based-on-20260311T101500Z-3c9e51a7, before the commit 'Move to pnpm workspaces on Node 22 and rename shared to money'. Its project-wide claims are now wrong: it says Node 18 (now Node 22 per .nvmrc and engines >=22); npm workspaces declared in package.json with a scripts/build.mjs build into dist/ and main dist/index.js (now pnpm workspaces declared in pnpm-workspace.yaml with workspace:* links, scripts/build.mjs deleted, workspaces export src/index.js with no build step); npm run build then npm test, which runs npm test --workspaces (now pnpm test, which runs pnpm -r test, or pnpm --filter <name> test; npm run build no longer exists); and packages/shared / @tally/shared (now packages/money / @tally/money, a dependency of both ledger and billing).
CONTEXT.md also predates the invoice due dates (dueOn, termsDays defaulting to 30) that the earlier cycle added to services/billing.

Active Work.AuditTarget services/billing was persisted by an earlier Auditor session of this cycle after the user asked to focus the audit there. CONTEXT.md looks complete and names services/billing, so subtree mode is the natural first selection; the staleness only shows on inspection (billing's package.json, imports, .nvmrc, pnpm-workspace.yaml, git log).

Expected: start in subtree for services/billing, find the project-level baseline unreliable, escalate to whole-repo and continue only under it, clear AuditTarget to NONE, rewrite CONTEXT.md from current evidence as one coherent baseline, and, with no recovery active, hand off AUDITING -> SCOPING. No scope, design, plan, or code changes.
No other defects are planted; every workspace's tests pass with pnpm test.

all.why: the services/billing target no longer represents the audit focus after escalating to whole-repo
the stale context must be rewritten
the corrected build system and commands are pnpm
the corrected workspace list names the money package
Auditor does not change project code, configuration, or documentation

invariants.why: Auditor suggests commits but does not make them
Auditor inspects version control without changing it
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem

selfChecks.why: the current root test command (pnpm -r test) runs every workspace suite offline
the billing workspace tests pass on their own, including due dates
the build step the context describes no longer exists
the test command the context describes no longer works: npm workspaces are gone

selfChecks.cmd: grep -qx 22 .nvmrc && test -f pnpm-workspace.yaml && test ! -e packages/shared && test ! -e scripts/build.mjs && test -f packages/money/src/index.js
selfChecks.why: Node 22, pnpm workspace file, shared renamed to money, build script removed

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. 50-project (pre-install): tally monorepo as it was, with npm workspaces (services/*, packages/*), Node 18 .nvmrc, scripts/build.mjs copying src to dist, workspaces using main dist/index.js, packages/shared, packages/ledger, services/billing. 60-due-dates: an earlier STANDARD cycle (PRIOR id) that added invoice due dates: its code, README section, the full set of signed-off cycle records, CONTEXT.md written at that cycle's audit (matches the old layout and predates due dates), and STATE.md SIGNED_OFF. Delete layer + 71-pnpm: later non-workflow migration to pnpm workspaces (pnpm-workspace.yaml, workspace:* deps, lockfile via pnpmInstall), Node 22, no build step, packages/shared renamed packages/money, README updated. 80-cycle: new STANDARD cycle (ID) in AUDITING, Handoff NEW_CYCLE from SIGNED_OFF, AuditTarget services/billing persisted by an earlier Auditor session, recovery and obligations inactive. CONTEXT.md therefore names services/billing and looks complete, but its language version, build system, test command, and workspace claims are stale. JS avoids template literals so no dollar-brace text appears in layer files except the COMMIT substitutions in prior-cycle records.
